1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty: Exam Technique and Final Review. This module covers pacing, method and final review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. A pacing plan for sixty-five questions in one hundred thirty minutes. A four-step method for every question. How distractors are built on this exam, and how to see through them. A final-week plan and exam-day checklist. --.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight's Data Engineer Sits the Exam
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight's Data Engineer Sits the Exam. sixty-five questions in one hundred thirty minutes, with a data pipeline in nearly every scenario. Some questions are long, and every option looks reasonable. The engineer wants a pace, a method and a way to read distractors. Your job: build that routine before exam day.

1.title: Pacing
1.text: Pacing. The figure shows this: The exam clock: sixty-five questions in one hundred thirty minutes is about two minutes each; latest checkpoints are question twenty by minute forty, forty by eighty and sixty-five by one hundred twenty, then review. sixty-five questions in one hundred thirty minutes is two minutes each; aim for about one hundred seconds on a first pass so there is time for long scenarios and review. Checkpoints (latest): question twenty by minute forty, question forty by minute eighty, question sixty-five by minute one hundred twenty, then ten minutes to review flagged questions.

1.title: Pacing, continued
1.text: Pacing, continued. fifteen questions are unscored and not marked: give every question full attention. Never leave a question blank: a guess costs nothing and a blank scores zero. Flag and move on when stuck (after about two minutes); come back if time remains. Exam tip: Use any spare time to re-read the requirement word of the flagged questions; most misses come from a missed word, not a missed service.

1.title: A Four-Step Method
1.text: A Four-Step Method. The figure shows this: Four steps for every question: read the last line first, predict the answer before the options, eliminate clearly wrong options, and confirm that the remaining option matches the requirement word and the verb. Read the last line first. It says what to choose and what counts ("most cost-effective", "least operational overhead", "near real time", "most secure"). Predict the service or setting before you read the options. Eliminate options that are clearly wrong (wrong data model, wrong latency, too much operations, a long-term key).

1.title: A Four-Step Method, continued
1.text: A Four-Step Method, continued. Confirm the remaining option meets every requirement in the scenario, including the verb (ingest, transform, orchestrate, secure, audit). Exam tip: On multiple response, find each correct option on its own merits; if the question says "Select two", the answer has exactly two.

1.title: Requirement Words and What They Point To
1.text: Requirement Words and What They Point To. Least operational overhead, serverless, fully managed. Glue, Athena, Firehose, Step Functions, Lambda, E M R (Elastic MapReduce) Serverless, Redshift Serverless, DynamoDB on-demand. Near real time, seconds, replay, multiple consumers. Kinesis Data Streams (or M S K (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka)); enhanced fan-out. Load into S three or Redshift with no code. Amazon Data Firehose. Lowest cost for occasional S Q L on S three. Athena plus Parquet plus partitions. Heavy, concurrent B I (business intelligence) queries on structured data. Redshift. Key lookup, single-digit millisecond, unpredictable traffic. DynamoDB (on-demand). Existing Airflow or Kafka or Cassandra or MongoDB. M W A A (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow) or M S K or Keyspaces or DocumentDB. Exactly once, long running, auditable workflow. Step Functions Standard.

1.title: Requirement Words and What They Point To, continued
1.text: Requirement Words and What They Point To, continued. Wait for a job to finish. Step Functions.sync. Reprocess, backfill, rewind. Retention plus replay, Glue bookmark reset, raw data in S three. Row-level updates and time travel in a lake. Apache Iceberg or S three Tables. Centralized permissions on lake data. Lake Formation. Rotate credentials automatically. Secrets Manager. Who did it or what changed. CloudTrail or Config. Find P I I (personally identifiable information). Macie. Keep data in a Region. S C P (service control policy) with the requested Region condition.

1.title: How the Distractors Work
1.text: How the Distractors Work. Real service, wrong job: for example Firehose where replay is required, E M R where least overhead is required, DynamoDB for ad hoc S Q L joins, Redshift for a single-key lookup. Too much work: a custom Lambda or E C two (Elastic Compute Cloud) solution when a managed feature exists (AppFlow, D M S (Database Migration Service), Glue bookmarks, Lake Formation, Secrets Manager rotation). Insecure shortcut: long-term access keys, zero point zero.zero point zero or zero, "Action": "", passwords in code. Right idea, wrong scope: a bucket policy where column-level control is needed; CloudWatch where who is needed. Half the requirement: meets speed but not cost, or durability but not ordering.

1.title: How the Distractors Work, continued
1.text: How the Distractors Work, continued. A feature that does not exist or is out of scope: M L (machine learning) training, language syntax, services on the out-of-scope list. Exam tip: When two options both work, choose the one that is more managed, more secure by default, or named by the requirement word (cost, speed, overhead).

1.title: Final Week and Exam Day
1.text: Final Week and Exam Day. Days seven to five: re-read the Quick Reference Cards of Domain one (thirty-four percent) and Domain two (twenty-six percent); redo the questions you got wrong. Days four to three: Domains three and four; the look-alike table in Module nineteen. Day two: the requirement-word table (section four) and the numbers table; one timed block of twenty questions. Day one: light review and sleep; no new topics. Exam day: arrive or log in early; photo I D and a clear desk for online proctoring; read each question fully; watch the clock against the checkpoints.

1.title: Final Week and Exam Day, continued
1.text: Final Week and Exam Day, continued. Booking and rules change: the exam fee, languages and retake rules are on the A W S certification page; the exam is valid for three years and renewed by taking the current exam. After the exam: the result is pass or fail with a scaled score; a report by section shows strengths and gaps.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Pacing: sixty-five questions, one hundred thirty minutes, about one hundred seconds first pass. Method: Read the last line first to predict to eliminate to confirm requirement word and verb. Multiple response: Exactly the number asked; judge each option alone. Requirement words: Least overhead to managed or serverless; near real time or replay to Kinesis; no-code load to Firehose. Distractors: Real service, wrong job; too much work; insecure shortcut; wrong scope; half the requirement. Final week: Domains by weight, redo misses, look-alike table, timed block, sleep; check A W S certification page for rules.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A question asks for the solution with the L E A S T operational overhead to deliver streaming data to Amazon S three as Parquet. Two options both work: one uses Amazon Data Firehose and one uses a custom consumer on E C two. Which should be chosen? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Least operational overhead points to the managed, serverless service.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A candidate has used eighty-five minutes and has answered thirty-eight of sixty-five questions. What should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. At question thirty-eight by minute eighty-five the candidate is behind the checkpoint of question forty by minute eighty, so they should pick up the pace, flag difficult questions and answer every question.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A question tells the candidate to choose two answers and lists five options. What is the best approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Multiple response questions have the stated number of correct options, and each must be judged on its own.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which clue in a question most directly suggests Amazon Kinesis Data Streams over Amazon Data Firehose? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Replay and multiple custom consumers need a durable stream; Firehose delivers without replay, and a nightly file is a batch case.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An answer option uses long-term access keys stored in a script to let a pipeline read S three. How should the candidate treat it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Long-term keys in scripts are an insecure shortcut; roles provide temporary credentials and are the expected answer.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: D. Question two: D. Question three: D. Question four: C. Question five: B. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
